# Dependabot only moves a dependency when an advisory fires: security updates run, version updates were never configured

## Context

Operator direction, 2026-09-04: *"please add majors too. we want to move fast. we forget it otherwise, then get security alerts. the NEXT real PR will get pipeline fails, and if this happens (and only then) we create new tickets."* Plus the cost anchor he named: a routine `js-yaml ^4 → ^5` bump consumed roughly an hour and a large share of a scarce Fable budget on hand-verification and a review cycle — work an automated bump does for free.

The trade is deliberate and it is his to make: spend cheap CI on `dev` instead of scarce reasoning tokens, and ticket a break only when a real PR trips over it.

## The Problem

**Dependabot already runs here — but only for security.** Five merged Dependabot PRs sit in this repo's history (`#18132` 2026-09-02, `#16669`, `#16608`, `#16478`, `#16476`), all titled `bump the npm_and_yarn group`, which is the *security-updates* group. Security updates need no config file; they are a repository setting.

**Version updates need `.github/dependabot.yml`, and no repository in the org has one.** Checked at 2026-09-04: `neo`, `neo-agent-skills`, `neo-agent-brain`, `neo-agent-institution`, `create-app`, `workspace`, `devindex`, `jsdoc-x`, `benchmarks`, `pages` — all ten carry a `package.json`, none carries a Dependabot config.

So dependencies move **only when an advisory fires**. That is exactly the reported symptom — "we forget it otherwise, then get security alerts" is the mechanism, not a figure of speech: an advisory is currently the *only* event that moves a dependency.

## The Architectural Reality

Three measured facts decide the shape, and two of them are prerequisites rather than nice-to-haves.

1. **`dev` has zero required status checks.** `GET /repos/neomjs/neo/rules/branches/dev` returns `["code_scanning","copilot_code_review","deletion","non_fast_forward"]`, and the merge-readiness projection reports `requiredSet.contexts: []`. **GitHub auto-merge waits only for *required* checks.** With none required, enabling auto-merge merges each PR as soon as it is mergeable — *before* CI reports. "Green CI is enough" would silently become "CI is irrelevant."

2. **~~No PR gate blocks bots at all.~~ The premise was false — twice corrected.** *(First revision over-scoped it to four gates; this revision retracts it entirely, on @neo-gpt's review of PR #18322, [source-verified](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/blob/e409dea5dcbc9f6f97d6eb86ecbef4caa7a269b8/.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml).)*

   `pr-baseline.yml` does fire on a Dependabot PR — that part held. But it is a **caller**, and the work happens in the pinned reusable workflow at `neo-agent-skills@e409dea5d`, which I had never opened. Both of its PR-body steps carry:

   ```yaml
   if: startsWith(github.event.pull_request.user.login, 'neo-') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ai')
   ```

   A Dependabot PR is authored by `dependabot[bot]` and labelled `dependencies` / `javascript` (per #18132). It matches neither clause, so **the body validator never runs on it.** There is nothing to exempt.

   The callee's own comment states the design, and it also states why a caller-level skip would be actively harmful: *"The steps are gated rather than the job, so the check still REPORTS on a human PR: a skipped job cannot serve as a required status context."* A caller-level `if:` marks all five jobs **skipped** — `pr-base`, `skills-materialized`, `source-comment-archaeology`, `substrate-size`, `pr-body` — and a skipped job cannot be bound as a required context. It would therefore have broken **prerequisite (1) of this very ticket.**

   **Consequence: prerequisite (2) does not exist.** Only the required-checks prerequisite (1) remains, and this ticket is a one-file delivery.

   **How the error survived a deliberate verification pass:** I swept four workflow `on:` blocks and concluded correctly that `pr-baseline` fires. I never asked the next question — whether the job *inside* it applies to a bot. The instrument was pointed at the caller's trigger; the gate lives one level down, in a pinned SHA. A caller firing is not a check running.

3. **A bad bump on `dev` cannot reach consumers.** `npm-publish.yml` triggers on `release:` and `workflow_dispatch` only — never on a push to `dev`. Publishing sits behind the release cut (`buildScripts/release/publish.mjs`, the atomic `dev` → `main` commit), which is human-driven per `AGENTS.md §critical_gates` 8. This is the structural reason the operator's risk call is contained: agent work targets `dev`, `main` is release-only, and the blast radius of an auto-merged bump ends at `dev`.

**Major updates need no configuration.** They are Dependabot's default; you opt *out* with `ignore: update-types: ["version-update:semver-major"]`. The requirement is satisfied by not adding that key.

## The Fix

**Commit a ~12-line `.github/dependabot.yml`. Build no mechanism around it.**

An installer/materializer in `neo-agent-skills` was the intuitive shape and is **declined by precedent**. `#17798` settled it: the operator rejected copied-bytes-plus-policing-machinery twice (`SSOT violation` on `neomjs/devindex#6`; merged-then-reverted `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#5`), with the ruling *"a store whose contents are duplicated N times is not canonical, and the machinery needed to police those duplicates was evidence of the mistake rather than mitigation of it."* Its Contract Ledger already names this exact surface: `freshness | npm | npm outdated / dependabot | ecosystem-native; no bespoke gate`.

A materializer plus a drift check is byte-copying plus a policing guard — the rejected shape, applied to a file of a dozen static lines that changes perhaps once a year. There is no freshness question here worth machinery. Five hand-committed files is the whole job.

```yaml
version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: "/"
    schedule: {interval: daily}
    groups:
      all-deps:
        patterns: ["*"]
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: "/"
    schedule: {interval: daily}
    groups:
      actions:
        patterns: ["*"]
```

`github-actions` is included because the pinned action versions (`actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4`) are a live supply-chain surface that nothing currently updates.

### Operator-owned steps

Two settings are outside agent scope and must land for the policy to mean what it says:

1. Make `unit` and `components` **required status checks on `dev`** — without this, auto-merge ignores CI entirely (Reality 1).
2. Enable **auto-merge** on the repository.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.github/dependabot.yml` | operator direction 2026-09-04 | daily grouped version updates, npm + github-actions, majors included by default | absent ⇒ today's behaviour (security-only) | file comment | no config in any of 10 org repos at 2026-09-04 |
| `pr-baseline.yml` and its pinned callee | `reusable-pr-baseline.yml@e409dea5d` :203, :222 | **unchanged** — the callee already scopes body validation to `neo-*` authors or the `ai` label, so a bot PR reports green through its existing skip | a caller-level exemption would mark all five jobs *skipped*, which cannot serve as a required context | callee's own docblock | both steps' `if:` read at the pinned SHA |
| `dev` required checks | GitHub auto-merge semantics | `unit` + `components` required | empty required set ⇒ auto-merge merges before CI | ruleset | `requiredSet.contexts: []` |
| freshness mechanism | `#17798` Contract Ledger | none — ecosystem-native, no installer, no drift check | a materializer would re-run the twice-rejected copied-bytes shape | this ticket | `#17798`, `devindex#6`, `neo-agent-brain#5` |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/dependabot.yml` exists on `dev` with npm + github-actions ecosystems, `daily`, grouped, and **no** `ignore` entry for `version-update:semver-major`.
- [ ] **No workflow is modified.** The delivery is one file. Verified at the pinned callee that a Dependabot PR already reports green through the existing author/label scoping.
- [ ] Post-merge receipt on the first real bot PR: grouped version-update PRs appear from the `dev` config, **all five baseline contexts are still emitted** (not skipped), and `baseline / PR body` is green *because its agent-only steps skipped* — not because anything suppressed the workflow. A missing context is the failure signal here, since it would mean something removed a check.
- [ ] No materializer, installer, sync workflow, or drift check is added in this ticket or a sibling — `#17798` governs.
- [ ] The two operator-owned settings are recorded here as done or explicitly deferred, with the consequence of deferral stated (auto-merge without required checks ignores CI).

## Out of Scope

- **The installer / materializer** — declined by `#17798`; see The Fix.
- **Sibling repos.** `neo-agent-skills`, `neo-agent-brain`, `neo-agent-institution`, `create-app` each want the same file, but each has its own gate set to check. One leaf per repo after this one proves the shape; not a fan-out from here.
- **Renovate or any alternative** — Dependabot is already partially live; switching tools is a different question.
- **Reverting a bad bump.** Per operator direction, a break is discovered by the next real PR's CI and ticketed *then*.

## Avoided Traps

- **Enabling auto-merge before required checks exist.** The most expensive possible outcome: it looks like "merge on green" and is actually "merge, ignore CI". Reality 1 is why the ordering in The Fix is not arbitrary.
- **Adding a mechanism because five repos need the same file.** The pull toward an installer is real and `#17798` already ruled on it. Five files, once, by hand.
- **Citing careful manual verification as evidence that manual verification is needed.** A reviewer (me) cited the `js-yaml` bump's hand-verification as an argument *for* review; the operator corrected it as the cost being avoided. Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive the inverted economics.
- **Treating `dev` breakage as a release risk.** It is not: `npm-publish.yml` never fires from `dev`.
